_comment: Player-facing vocabulary. World bible sections 1, 9 and 10. Change a word here and it changes everywhere. One word per idea, at Sean's word of 17 September: a person of yours is CREW and never an officer or personnel; talking a place round is a PARLEY and never diplomacy; and the three things you can be looking at are the WORLD MAP, a REACH MAP and a LOCATION. In prose a location is still an island, because in this world it is one - what is forbidden is a second word for the same idea in a label. A ground unit is a TROOP, plural TROOPS, at Sean's word of 19 September - "rename 'company' to 'troop(s)' through game when talking about ground units" - which reverses the 17 September ruling that made it COMPANY and retired troops. Company is the retired word now. A troop is raised at a BARRACKS at Sean's word of 20 September - "Change 'Training Facilities' to 'Barracks' across game" - so 'training facility' is retired too. The key stays `training_facility`, the way `refinery` stays the key for the Lumber Mill: ids are code and labels are words.

facilityBlurbs.mine: Sinks a shaft on a vein of gold. Nothing else in the Seven Seas earns like it, and few islands have the ground for one.
facilityBlurbs.silver_mine: Sinks a shaft on a seam of silver. Twice what a mill earns, and there is a good deal more silver about than gold.
facilityBlurbs.refinery: Cuts and works the standing timber. Wants a forest under it, and most islands have a few.
facilityBlurbs.coral_kiln: Works the living coral for lime and building stone. Wants a coral bed under it, and only Coral Reach has them.
facilityBlurbs.training_facility: Drills marines and militia. Every troop you raise comes off this floor.
facilityBlurbs.shipyard: Lays down hulls. Nothing to build here until the fleets arrive.
facilityBlurbs.fort: A battery on the harbor wall. Fires on any enemy hull lying off the island, whether or not you have a fleet there, and no landing can be made while one still stands.
facilityBlurbs.heavy_fort: The same wall built twice over: more than twice the guns and two and a half times the stone, on the one plot a Fortress would have taken. Costs more per gun than two Fortresses would, and is the only answer on an island with no room left.
